name: Andorra
headline: Andorra's single shared record links almost all care and patients can read results in an app, but opting out is hard and fines are low.

access.summary: Llei 20/2017 gives a right to the whole record, with copies within five working days. The national Andorra Salut app shows reports, test results and vaccinations, but it needs a digital certificate and has about 25,000 users.
detail: Article 43 of Llei 20/2017 gives the patient access to the clinical record and all the documents in it. The patient must be informed of its content within five working days at most, and copies are delivered in the same period.
Subjective notes by professionals are not part of the record, so the patient has no right to see them unless the author agrees (Article 44). Data about third persons can be withheld.

The Andorra Salut app, created in 2021, shows medical reports, test results, vaccination records and appointments (WHO Observatory, 2026). A February 2026 update added pending referrals and tests, and a QR code to share results with doctors outside Andorra.

The government reported over 50,000 downloads, 25,000 users and about 5,000 connections a month. Access requires a digital certificate. We did not verify an official figure on the share of residents who use it, or a machine-readable export.

control.summary: The law lets a patient block clinicians' direct access to the shared record and get a log of every access within 15 working days. The log comes only on request, and in 2019 patients asking to leave were told no real alternative existed.
detail: Article 39.2 of Llei 20/2017 lets the patient deny direct access to the shared record. The denial applies to every professional, so there is no choice by professional or by document.

Article 32.2 gives a right to a copy of the access trail of the shared record within 15 working days. Article 34.8 adds immediate access to the trail when the national commission finds an unjustified access. We found no log the patient can see in the app.
Objection, correction and deletion rights can be refused in the general interest or for the person's own health (Article 34.7).

In December 2019 Altaveu, citing unnamed sources, reported that patients who asked to leave the shared record were told the alternative did not exist and were put on a monitored list instead. We found no newer evidence. A log on request plus an opt-out not shown to work puts the score at the top of the 40 to 55 band.

privacy.summary: Llei 29/2021 mirrors the GDPR, with 72-hour breach notice, and the EU recognises Andorra as adequate. But fines stop at 100,000 euros, public bodies such as the public health service can only be warned, and the one recent health case we found ended in warnings.
detail: Article 9 of Llei 29/2021 bans processing health, genetic and biometric data except on listed grounds, such as explicit consent or care. Breaches must be reported to the APDA within 72 hours where possible.
Fines run from 500 euros to 100,000 euros for the most serious cases (Article 73). Under Article 74, public bodies and parapublic entities are only warned, not fined.

In July 2025 the APDA issued warnings to two psychology centres over the irregular transfer and keeping of clinical files. Llei 20/2017 adds health-specific fines up to 100,000 euros for unjustified access to clinical data.
The European Commission lists Andorra among countries with an adequacy decision. A new APDA head took office in October 2025 and named filling the vacant inspector post as a priority.

commercial.summary: Andorran health law treats giving clinical data to third parties as a very serious offence, with fines up to 100,000 euros. We found no specific rule on health apps, data brokers or insurers' use of health data beyond the general data law.
detail: Article 32 of Llei 20/2017 gives every user the right that their data are not passed to third parties, except where the law allows. Article 57 makes the transfer of clinical or social data to third parties a very serious offence, fined 50,001 to 100,000 euros (Article 59).
Llei 29/2021 requires explicit consent or another listed ground for health data, and gives a right to object at any time to direct marketing (Article 24).
We found no Andorran rule specific to consumer health apps, data brokers or the sale of de-identified health data. The low fine ceiling limits deterrence for large firms.

journey.summary: One national shared record links the public hospital, primary care and all clinical labs, and a July 2026 decree makes it the main tool for referrals. E-prescription was still in a pilot announced for April 2026.
detail: Llei 20/2017 creates a single shared clinical record for the public system, and every authorised centre and professional must record their care in it (Article 41).
Care received abroad that the social security fund (CASS) reimburses is not repaid until the information is added to the shared record (Article 41.6).

In February 2024 the health minister said all clinical labs and three of four imaging centres were integrated; the fourth was under investigation. Decret 305/2026 routes internal referrals through the record and calls it the main coordination tool.

The health minister said an e-prescription pilot would start within ten days of 12 April 2026, with rollout after the summer. Whether it reached all prescribers and pharmacies by September 2026 was not verified.

clinical.summary: Any professional authorised in Andorra can open the shared record with a stated reason, and the patient's own doctor without one. Doctors in Spain and France, where some care takes place, are not connected and rely on patient-shared QR codes.
detail: Under Article 41.4 of Llei 20/2017, all health professionals authorised to practise in Andorra have access to the shared record. They give a reason for access, except the patient's referring doctor.
Treating professionals have direct and immediate access according to their profile (Article 39.1), unless the patient has denied it.
The WHO Observatory says the shared record supports a GP-led care pathway across levels of care. Some specialist and tertiary care is provided in France and Spain.
Since February 2026 the app lets patients share test results through a QR code with doctors who are not connected to the Andorran record.

research.summary: Identifiable record data cannot be used for research without express written consent, and an ethics committee must approve research on people. Use with identities removed needs no consent and has no opt-out.
detail: Article 51 of Llei 20/2017 bars research use of identifiable record data without full information and express written consent. Breaking this is a serious offence (Article 56).

Article 40.4 allows record access for studies, research and planning if identifying data are protected, unless the person consented. Health ministry staff may use named data for public health surveillance.
All research on people in Andorra must be approved by the Research Ethics Committee (Article 48.6). Staff with access owe secrecy (Article 40.5).
We found no public register of research uses and no general opt-out. Four safeguard classes count, which reaches the cap of 50.

ai.summary: Andorra has a 2024 government AI ethics code, required only for some public-sector processes, and signed the Council of Europe AI convention, but no AI law or clinical AI rules we could find. How AI medical devices are regulated was not verified.
detail: In May 2024 the government approved an AI ethics code for the public sector, companies and citizens. Adherence is required of the public sector for some processes and voluntary for others.
Andorra signed the Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI on 5 September 2024. We did not verify ratification.
Andorra is not in the EU or EEA, so the EU AI Act does not apply. We could not verify whether Andorra requires CE marking or its own approval for AI used as a medical device.

No health-specific AI guidance was found. With no verified device rule for AI, the score sits in the 15 to 30 band for non-EU countries with no clinical AI rules, at its top for the ethics code and the treaty signature.
